issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Rideable.messageOnRide() to be a parameterless method returning a String (see UML and example usage in Main which calls r.messageOnRide()). However, the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it with an int parameter in Pig and Seal. This parameter mismatch changes the method signature and expected usage, causing compile errors or behavioral differences if students follow the problem/template (which call messageOnRide() with no arguments).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and its implementations consistent with the problem/template. Either (A) change the solution to define messageOnRide() with no parameters and return the string "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (adjust Pig and Seal accordingly), or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnRide(int speed) and document the speed parameter and expected output. Preferred: modify the solution to remove the int parameter so it matches the UML and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() on the Rideable interface (and implementations) but the solution repository defines messageOnRide(int speed) (interface and implementing classes). This mismatch in the method signature/parameterization prevents a direct mapping from the exercise description/template usage (e.g., calls to r.messageOnRide()) to the solution code and will confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable API with the problem/template by removing the int parameter: declare String messageOnRide() in Rideable and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Update any calls accordingly (e.g., r.messageOnRide()).
